name: Employment visa and Iqama (kafala-based sponsored work permit)

requirements.blocker_text: Requires a job offer from a Saudi-registered employer (the kafeel/sponsor), who secures a block-visa quota and initiates the work-permit application via the Qiwa platform before the worker enters the country.
requirements.fix_path: Secure a job offer from a Saudi employer with available Nitaqat (Saudization) quota headroom to sponsor a foreign worker.

requirements.blocker_text: Since the July 2025 reform, every role is classified into one of three tiers under the Saudi Standard Classification of Occupations (SSCO) -- High-Skilled (degree plus 5 years' experience, doctors/engineers/executives), Skilled (secondary education plus relevant experience, technicians), or Basic -- each with different salary and documentation requirements, automatically gated through the Qiwa platform.
requirements.fix_path: Confirm the employer has correctly classified the role in Qiwa and that the applicant's qualifications match the claimed tier.

requirements.blocker_text: High-Skilled tier roles require a documented salary of at least SAR 15,000/month, in addition to a relevant degree and 5+ years of experience; Skilled and Basic tiers have lower, role-dependent thresholds.
requirements.fix_path: Negotiate a salary meeting the applicable SSCO tier threshold, or apply under a lower tier if the role qualifies.

evidence_required.document: Employment contract classified in Qiwa under the correct SSCO tier
Medical examination at a GCC-approved clinic before travel
Degree attestation and, for High-Skilled roles, proof of 5+ years' relevant experience

outcome.duration_length: 1-2 years, renewed annually with the Iqama, tied to the employment contract

sources.title: Qiwa (Ministry of Human Resources and Social Development's official labour platform) -- work permit and SSCO skill-tier classification
Ministry of Interior -- General Directorate of Passports (Jawazat), residence permit (Iqama) issuance and renewal, corroborating the annual renewal cycle

notes: STRUCTURAL FINDING: this is the biggest single procedural overhaul found anywhere in the Saudi build. In July 2025, HRSD replaced the old binary 'professional vs. non-professional' work-permit model with a three-tier Saudi Standard Classification of Occupations (SSCO) system -- High-Skilled, Skilled, Basic -- enforced automatically within the Qiwa platform, with all existing permits transitioned into the new system by late 2025. Several English-language secondary sources dated even mid-2026 still describe the old professional/non-professional binary as current, the same live-staleness failure mode caught repeatedly elsewhere in this dataset (Poland's Type A/B/C renaming, UK/Germany/Netherlands salary re-basings). pr_after_months is left null and leads_to_pr is true only in the narrow sense that this route can lead toward Premium Residency (not a traditional PR ladder) or the fully discretionary naturalisation track (see sa_naturalisation) -- Saudi Arabia has no ordinary points-in-time permanent-residence status comparable to the other 14 countries in this dataset; the closest functional equivalent is Premium Residency, which this route's switchable_to correctly points to rather than to a plain 'permanent residence' route that does not exist here. citizenship_after_months (120) reflects the general 10-year naturalisation residence minimum under Royal Decree No. M/88, chained from this route -- see sa_naturalisation for the full, heavily discretionary detail; this figure should be read as a floor, not a realistic expectation, since approval is administratively rare regardless of years served.
